source_text: Colligit autem Apostolus et pronuntiat esse alios, qui peccaverint sicut Adam, alios, quos nec similitudo antiquae praevaricationis asperserit; absolute ergo claret morum crimina esse, non seminum. Atque ut breviter quae sunt acta repetamus, ait Apostolus per unum hominem intrasse peccatum. Hoc ratio ostendit imitationi, non generationi congruere, quae est opus duorum.
pass_a_gloss: But the Apostle collects and pronounces that there are some who have sinned as Adam, others whom not even a likeness of the ancient transgression has sprinkled; it is therefore absolutely clear that they are crimes of manners, not of seeds. And that we may briefly repeat the things which have been done, the Apostle says that sin entered through one human being. This reason shows fits imitation, not generation, which is a work of two.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: But the apostle concludes and declares that some sinned as Adam did, while others were not even touched by the likeness of the ancient transgression. It is therefore perfectly clear that these are crimes of conduct, not of seed. To repeat our results briefly: the apostle says sin entered through one man (Romans 5:12). Reason shows that this fits imitation, not generation, which is the work of two.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
